title: Pinebloom preflight: on‑prem handoff + dry‑run checklist (weekly prep)
content:
Purpose:
- Prep notes for the weekly customer sync (Pinebloom). Focus: final preflight before customer dry‑run next week (Wed 2025-02-26).
- Capture outstanding blockers, owners, clear asks to customer, and a rollback/fallback plan.

Meeting goals (30m):
1) Validate dry‑run plan & window (Wed 02/26 02:00–05:00 PST). Confirm Pinebloom ops on standby.
2) Walk through infra checklist (VPC peering, route tables, firewall rules, DNS certs).
3) Confirm app deployment order + migration step owners.
4) Surface last blockers and assign clear owners with deliverable dates.
5) Agree on post‑dry‑run verification checks and rollback triggers.

Quick status snapshot (what I want to say first):
- Control plane: green — control plane API reachable from customer VPC via transit gateway.
- Data plane: amber — one kube node in edge cluster still failing kubelet registration intermittently (infra ticket JIRA-PNB-4021).
- Certs: amber — cert rotation script created but missing SAN for internal metrics host (PR #87).
- Migration scripts: ready, need final smoke test in staging with larger seq len (Samir owns).

Top blockers (priority order):
1) Kubelet registration flakiness (JIRA-PNB-4021) — impact: can cause pod eviction during dry‑run.
   - Current hypothesis: antrea CNI mtu mismatch with customer overlay + slow DHCP on boot.
   - Temporary mitigation: pin pod disruption budget, add node readiness delay (5m).
   - Owner: Samir Patel. ETA for mitigation script: 2025-02-22 EOD.

2) TLS cert SAN mismatch for metrics endpoint (blocked PR #87).
   - Impact: monitoring agent will fail TLS handshake; we won't have perf metrics during dry‑run.
   - Short term: allow insecure skip for metrics agent (customer ok?) — must confirm.
   - Owner: Jamal Rivera (infra) + Pinebloom SRE (customer). Target PR merge: 2025-02-21.

3) Cross‑account IAM role mapping: missing assume role in customer account for log shipper.
   - Impact: no logs to central ELK during test.
   - Owner: Ellen Park (solutions eng) to coordinate with customer security. Needed by 2025-02-24.

4) DB migration dry‑run staging data size mismatch — test data is 1/10th production causing caching behavior differences.
   - Impact: cannot validate long‑tail latency.
   - Owner: Lena Morales (me). Workaround: load generation script to simulate tail load. ETA: 2025-02-24.

Runbook highlights to review in meeting:
- Sequence: (1) vpc-peering verification (2) infra bootstrap (nodes ready) (3) deploy control plane (4) enable routing rules (5) push model artifacts (6) run traffic generator (smoke tests) (7) monitor metrics 30m and switch live.
- Rollback triggers: >10% error rate on 5m rolling window OR CPU >85% sustained 3m on model nodes OR failed healthchecks >3/5.
- Rollback method: scale replica count to previous commit + reapply previous config, then disable routing to new cluster.

Preflight checklist (quick tick boxes to run through live):
- [ ] Customer point of contact (ops oncall confirmed) — name + number
- [ ] Scheduled maintenance window + approval in change control
- [ ] VPC peering routes present and validated using traceroute
- [ ] Security group rules: egress to control plane + ingress for health checks
- [ ] TLS certs cover metrics+admin hosts (verify openssl s_client)
- [ ] IAM roles for log shipping configured and tested
- [ ] NFS mount (if used) tested with 10MB file write/read
- [ ] Disk pressure baseline collected for the last 24h
- [ ] Model artifact checksum verified (sha256)
- [ ] Dry‑run traffic generator configured (rps pattern file attached)
- [ ] Observability alerts mapped to oncall escalation numbers

Action items (assignments & dates):
- Samir: push kubelet readiness delay + mitigation playbook (JIRA-PNB-4021) — due 2025-02-22.
- Jamal: merge cert PR #87 OR produce documented exception for metrics agent — due 2025-02-21.
- Ellen: finalize cross‑account IAM and test logshipper — due 2025-02-24.
- Lena: run synthetic tail load script in staging and post results to Slack #pinebloom-deploy — due 2025-02-24.
- Customer (Pinebloom SRE - Casey): confirm ops oncall and approve maintenance window — due 2025-02-21.

Notes to self (things to call out in sync):
- Ask customer about accepting a short metrics exception (only for dry‑run) vs delaying dry‑run. Prioritize observability but don't block launch if infra can tolerate short window.
- Emphasize rollback safety — get verbal approval for rollback triggers during call.
- Keep the conversation concrete: call out who hits which button (names and Slack handles).

Open questions / decisions needed now:
- Can Pinebloom accept metrics insecure skip for 2 hours during dry‑run? (Customer decision)
- If kubelet flakiness repeats during dry‑run, do we abort immediately or try mitigation and continue? (ask for escalation authority)
- Does legal need to sign a short exception for cross‑account role for log shipping? (Ellen to check)

Dry‑run verification checklist (post‑deploy 30m):
- 2000 sample requests through gateway, <2% 5xx errors
- Latency p50/p95/p99 within agreed thresholds (p95 <= 350ms)
- Model inference error rate (invalid responses) <1%
- Logs present in central ELK for 10 minutes after traffic start
- Key metrics dashboard (latency/cpu/mem/queue depth) populated

Prep notes for the meeting opener (script):
- 0–2m: quick status, confirm participants and window
- 2–8m: run through top blockers & expected mitigations (owner, ETA)
- 8–18m: infra checklist and runbook sequence — call for thumbs up
- 18–26m: action items and signoffs (who approves rollback)
- 26–30m: confirm next steps, schedule dry‑run war room (Slack channel + Zoom)

Post‑meeting follow up (what I will do immediately):
- Update the Confluence runbook with any signoffs and owner ETAs.
- Create/update JIRA tickets with exact acceptance criteria and due dates.
- DM owners to remind about deadlines and ask for any blockers by EOD tomorrow.

Random scratch (reminders to myself):
- Bring up the possibility of a short warmup traffic ramp (0→50→200 rps over 10m) to reduce chaos.
- Check NTP sync on customer nodes; seen issues before causing schedule drift.
- Bring up cost implication if we extend dry‑run window — surface to customer finance if they push for longer.

End of doc.
